document_check.note: Zhang Q, Li J, Bian M, He Q, Shen Y, Lan Y, Huang D, 'Retinal Imaging Techniques Based on Machine Learning Models in Recognition and Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment', Neuropsychiatr Dis Treat 2021;17:3267-3281. AUC 0.87 is the SVM on original fundus images, MCI group, validation set (pp. 8, 10). The MCI group is mostly post-stroke (19 of 26) and older than controls (55.6 vs 35.1 years; Table 1, p. 9).

cited_result: AUC 0.87 for the MCI group (validation set) of an SVM classifier trained on HOG features from original fundus photographs, in a three-group (normal, MCI, dementia) rehabilitation-department sample of 86 participants.
tool_reason: The cited result is the discrimination (AUC) of a machine-learning classifier (SVM on image features) for diagnosing MCI, which is diagnostic model performance.

domains.rationale: The study is labelled cross-sectional, but recruitment is not described as consecutive, and the diagnostic groups came from different subpopulations. Controls were all non-stroke with mean age 35. The MCI and dementia groups were mostly stroke patients with mean age 55 to 58. This behaves like a case-control design, and age and stroke status are confounded with the diagnostic label.

domains.rationale: The MCI label rests on explicit cut-offs from standard instruments, assessed on the same day by trained staff, and does not use the fundus features. However, the rule combining those cut-offs is specific to this study ('clinical experts' advice'). The rule separating normal from dementia is not stated. No blinding is described.

The rest of the subjects were classified into the normal group or cognitive impairment group.

domains.rationale: The MCI group is tiny (26 participants: 17 training, 9 validation) against 3600 HOG features. Several images per participant were analysed as if independent, and the unit of the ten-fold cross-validation is not stated. No calibration measure is reported, although the discussion claims good calibration. Hyperparameters and class-imbalance handling are not reported. Validation is internal only (a random 2:1 split). A t-test across three group AUCs is used to compare models.

applicability.rationale: A rehabilitation sample with mostly post-stroke MCI and very young non-stroke controls does not match community or memory-clinic MCI screening.

The MCI label comes from a study-specific scale rule and largely reflects post-stroke cognitive impairment. The per-group AUC comes from a three-class task whose one-versus-rest construction is not described.

overall_rationale: Participants (domain 1) and analysis (domain 4) are both high. Controls differ sharply from cases in age and stroke status. There are 26 MCI cases for 3600 features, images are clustered within participants, calibration was not assessed, and there was no external validation. Under PROBAST, any high domain makes the overall rating high.
